native_result.query: In which century did the Diversity in Pottery Form collapses and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneuosly?
native_result.HypoA: Around 1800 BCE, Diversity in Pottery Form collapses, while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases.
native_result.HypoB: Diversity in Pottery Form collapsed and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increased simultaneously in the 17th century BCE (1700-1601 BCE; CE -1700 to -1601, calBP 3650-3551, 'the 1700s BCE'). At the 1700 BCE 100-year anchor PotteryForm drops 0.74 -> -1.13 (dZ = -1.87, -1.9 SD, the series floor, sustained 13 bins to 500 BCE) while PotteryDecoration rises -0.48 -> +0.97 (dZ = +1.45, +1.6 SD, above mean and p80, sustained to the end of the record, stepping to +1.53 at 1000 BCE). The level criterion (overlap 1700-500 BCE) and the one-bin rate criterion (Form dZ <= -1SD with Decoration dZ >= +1SD in the same bin) select the same century, and three of four Decoration threshold variants agree; only the strictest variant (Decoration >= mean+1SD) shifts the level overlap to 1000-500 BCE (10th c. BCE), which reflects a secondary Decoration step on an already-collapsed Form series. This is a cultural reorganisation (form diversity at its floor while decorative diversity peaks) at the terminal Late Neolithic / Older Bronze Age transition rather than a demographic crash: pollen openness (MEAN 2.42 -> 2.13; Belau_PC1_inter 1.66 -> 1.87; pollen_grate_100 +0.00069) shows no coeval collapse.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspected the three staged files: time_series_data.csv 3601 annual rows (CE -4100..-500, calBP = 1950-CE); all Z columns carry exactly 37 non-null anchors at exact 100-yr spacing with no gaps; _inter columns are verified exact linear interpolation (max dev 2e-16) hence no added information; capital.csv (comma decimals) matched the anchors exactly after CE = -BCE (max |diff| = 0) with only BCE 4300/4200 unmatched. 2) Computed anchor-level statistics (Form mean 0.062/sd 0.989/p20 -1.13; Deco mean 0.105/sd 0.917/p80 0.97). 3) FORM level criterion (<= mean-1SD, runs >=3 bins) -> 1700-500 BCE; FORM rate criterion (one-bin dZ <= -1SD) -> 1700 BCE only. 4) DECO variants V1 > mean, V2 >= p80, V3 >= mean+1SD, V4 directional (pre-3 mean <= 0.05, post-3 mean >= 0.30, positive step at t, whole post-window positive) with >=3-bin run filter. 5) Intersected Form runs with each Deco run (BCE intervals), printed the qualifying-bin table incl. the 1900-1400 BCE neighbourhood, explicitly excluded the 4000 BCE Decoration rise (Form rises +2.36 there) and the 2800 BCE Form drop (Deco falls). 6) Rate x Rate same-bin check. 7) Century conversion under the strict convention plus common usage, with right-truncation at the 500 BCE last anchor noted. 8) Sensitivity: 300-yr centred MA of anchors (onset shifts to 1600 BCE), 101-yr rolling mean of _inter (labelled artefact, unused), min-duration 1/2/3/5 bins. 9) Pollen openness used descriptively only. Scripts: analysis_00_inspection.py, analysis_02_events.py; outputs: main_analysis_log.txt, anchor_table.csv, results_summary.md.
